name: Question 13
problem:
Find the eigenvectors of the $2\times 2$ matrix $E$ given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}]E=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
Notice that the matrix $[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}]$ appears on both sides of the equation. Since this matrix is invertible (its determinant is not zero), left-multiplying the equation by the inverse gives the following expression for $E:$

$$
E={{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Therefore, $E$ is diagonalizable. The eigenvalues of $E$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ and the corresponding eigenvectors are the columns of the matrix $P.$ Computing $P,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}P={[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, the corresponding eigenvectors are: 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$

Question 13

Find the eigenvectors of the 2×2 matrix E given that [1154]E=[3002][1154].

a
[4−5] and [−21]
b
[−41] and [5−4]
c
[−54] and [1−1]
d
[15] and [14]
e
[−45] and [1−1]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that the matrix [1154] appears on both sides of the equation. Since this matrix is invertible (its determinant is not zero), left-multiplying the equation by the inverse gives the following expression for E:

E=[1154]−1⏟P[3002]⏟D[1154]⏟P−1

Therefore, E is diagonalizable. The eigenvalues of E are λ1=3 and λ2=2 and the corresponding eigenvectors are the columns of the matrix P. Computing P, we obtain

P=[1154]−1=1−1[4−1−51]=[−415−1].

In conclusion, the corresponding eigenvectors are:

v1=[−45] and v2=[1−1]
